name: Ruby on Rails
summary: A Ruby web application framework that composes applications from railties and engines, executes ordered initialization, and exposes routing, middleware, and convention-driven code loading as shared boundaries.

features.name: Railtie and engine composition
features.description: Rails::Application inherits from Rails::Engine, and engines and railties contribute configuration, paths, routes, middleware, and initializers to the host application.
benefits: Packages reusable capabilities behind framework extension boundaries
Allows mounted engines to contribute routes and isolated behavior
costs: Initialization order and host/engine interactions become application behavior
Mounted engines coordinate paths, routes, middleware, and configuration with the host

features.name: Ordered application initialization
features.description: Rails runs bootstrap, railtie, engine, application, middleware, eager-loading, and finishing callbacks in an ordered initialization process before the application serves requests.
benefits: Provides callback boundaries for environment-specific preparation
costs: Initialization dependencies are sensitive to callback ordering
Startup work and eager loading increase boot cost

features.name: Convention-driven code loading
features.description: Rails configures autoload and autoload-once paths for applications and engines, with reloadable code managed through framework autoloaders during development.
costs: Constant naming and directory conventions constrain correctness
Reloading exposes lifecycle and object-identity assumptions

features.name: Rack routing and middleware boundary
features.description: Rails builds a middleware stack around an application endpoint, dispatches controller actions through that stack, and combines application and engine route sets.
benefits: Composes request concerns around a common boundary
Separates route selection from cross-cutting middleware
costs: Multiple route sets increase dispatch reasoning cost

mathematical_views.question: Which configuration and loading transitions must complete before a Rails application is ready?
assumptions: Bootstrap, initializer, middleware, eager-loading, and finishing phases are ordered states
The view abstracts individual callback implementations and does not prove successful startup

mathematical_views.model: Typed engine and railtie composition graph
mathematical_views.question: How do applications, engines, railties, routes, paths, and initializers contribute to one runnable application?
assumptions: Applications, engines, and railties are vertices with contribution edges
The graph describes structural composition, not historical influence

mathematical_views.question: How do middleware layers transform or delegate a request before controller action execution?
assumptions: Each middleware is modeled as a function around a downstream Rack endpoint
Composition order follows the built stack
This is explanatory and does not assert invertibility

benefits: Reusable extensions contribute to a host application
costs: Cross-component lifecycle interactions expand integration surface
Ordering makes boot failures harder to localize

benefits: Less explicit loading code and development reloads

costs: Stack order and route mounts increase request-path complexity
